doc.title: Al Vollmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 8, 2017

title: Haywood Henry's death and top musicians without jobs
summary: Haywood Henry died of a heart attack after calling about his denture; Vollmer laments that great musicians were not respected.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Well yes. Some of it was quite shocking. Haywood Henry was in the band and Haywood had a sore spot on his lower denture. And he called while I went home to lunch. I had two houses. I kept the house where I had the office, and I bought this other big house five or six minutes away. And I went home for lunch. I came back and I knew that Haywood had called around 1:00 in the afternoon. And I had so many patients waiting for me when I got back that I had to see them all. I didn’t get to call Haywood’s home until 5:00 that afternoon. And I got his wife and she said, “Haywood’s dead.” So he had had a massive heart attack. She said he was sitting in bed reading the newspaper, the newspaper flew © Fillius Jazz Archive -12-

out of his hands and he had a massive heart attack and he was gone. Now I was amazed that Haywood joined the band, because he was a big name. Haywood was something else. But you know, the distressing part is that I’m an amateur and I’m not aggressive, and here are these guy who are at the top of their profession, and they are not respected, they don’t have jobs, and here they are they can join me.
